titleText.es: Mierda. No sólo no me lo instaló, sino que me suturó una pegatina en el brazo diciendo
titleText.en: Damn. Not only did he not install it, he sutured a 'Vista-Ready' sticker onto my arm.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive title attribute is genuinely truncated after diciendo because unescaped nested quotation marks terminate the HTML attribute; this field preserves that archive value exactly. The official English title text is complete and copied exactly. The raster's two USB labels remain explicit non-Spanish technical exclusions, while the surrounding Spanish technical vocabulary stays clickable.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: is; am; are (special estar helper for an ongoing action)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Esté is a subjunctive form of estar. Before an -ando or -iendo form, it helps present an ongoing action inside a pending, uncertain, or otherwise non-established situation.

example.es: Llámame mientras esté viajando.
example.en: Call me while I am traveling.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: operating; performing surgery
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Operando is the -ando form of operar. In a medical setting, operar means performing surgery on someone.

example.es: La cirujana está operando al paciente.
example.en: The surgeon is operating on the patient.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: can you; could you (formal or polite request)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In a question to one person addressed formally as usted, ¿puede + action? can make a polite request. Puede has the same written form used for he, she, or it.

example.es: ¿Puede abrir la ventana?
example.en: Could you open the window?

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to implant in me; to put inside my body
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Implantar is the unchanged dictionary form, and me attaches to identify the speaker as the person receiving the implant.

example.es: Van a implantarme un pequeño sensor.
example.en: They are going to implant a small sensor in me.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: port; computer connection socket
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In computing and electronics, a puerto is a physical or logical connection point. Elsewhere puerto can mean a harbor.

example.es: El portátil tiene un puerto libre.
example.en: The laptop has a free port.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: connect it (formal singular command)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Conecte is the command for one person addressed as usted, and lo stands for the masculine item being connected. Lo attaches to the command, and the written accent keeps the original stress.

example.es: Conéctelo a la pantalla.
example.en: Connect it to the screen.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to; introduces what something is connected to
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After conectar, a introduces the device, network, point, or other target receiving the connection.

example.es: Conecta el cable a la batería.
example.en: Connect the cable to the battery.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: nerves
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Nervios can name the body's nerves. In other contexts, tener nervios or estar nervioso describes nervousness.

example.es: Los nervios transmiten señales.
example.en: Nerves transmit signals.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: of; links consciente to what someone is aware of
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish uses consciente de before the fact, issue, or situation that a person knows about. A following que can introduce a complete fact.

example.es: Soy consciente de que falta tiempo.
example.en: I am aware that time is short.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: you; marks the formal person who is allowed to do something
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With permitir, le identifies one person affected by the permission. Here that person is the formally addressed listener; English normally places “you” directly before the allowed action.

example.es: La tarjeta le permitirá entrar.
example.en: The card will allow you to enter.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: will allow; will permit
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Permitirá keeps the whole dictionary form permitir and adds -á for one future subject or formal listener.

example.es: El pase permitirá abrir la puerta.
example.en: The pass will allow the door to be opened.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to control; to operate
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Controlar is the unchanged dictionary form. For machinery or devices, it means directing how they work.

example.es: El mando sirve para controlar el motor.
example.en: The controller is used to operate the motor.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: devices
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Dispositivos is the masculine plural of dispositivo, a device or piece of equipment designed for a purpose.

example.es: Apaga los dispositivos electrónicos.
example.en: Turn off the electronic devices.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: hardware; the physical parts of a computer or electronic system
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Hardware is a standard technical borrowing in Spanish. It contrasts with software, the programs and instructions rather than the physical equipment.

example.es: El fallo está en el hardware.
example.en: The fault is in the hardware.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: rest; remainder
cardDefinitions.noteEn: El resto names everything left after the already mentioned part has been separated out.

example.es: Guardaremos el resto para mañana.
example.en: We will save the rest for tomorrow.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: there will be
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Habrá is the future existence form of haber. It uses the irregular future stem habr- plus -á and stays singular even when what will exist is plural.

example.es: Habrá más opciones mañana.
example.en: There will be more options tomorrow.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to add to it; to give it an added feature
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Añadir is the unchanged dictionary form, and le attaches to identify the thing receiving the addition.

example.es: Queremos añadirle una función al programa.
example.en: We want to add a feature to the program.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: known; found out (completed-action form)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sabido is the completed-action form of saber. With a form of haber, it describes having learned or found out something.

example.es: ¿Cómo lo has sabido?
example.en: How did you find out?

cardDefinitions.promptEs: mientras + subjuntivo para una acción pendiente
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say “while” when the action is still pending or presented as a future possibility?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use mientras, then put the pending action's verb in a subjunctive form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Use ordinary present forms for a routine or established overlap, but use the subjunctive when the “while” action has not happened yet or is presented as a requested future situation. A progressive action can use a subjunctive form of estar plus an -ando/-iendo form.

example.es: Te escribiré mientras estés viajando.
example.en: I will write to you while you are traveling.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: Where does a short object pronoun go in a positive formal command?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Attach the pronoun to the end of the usted command and write the result as one word.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Use the formal command first, then attach me, te, lo, la, le, nos, los, las, or les as needed. Add a written accent when required to preserve the command's original stress: conecte + lo becomes conéctelo.

example.es: Firme el documento y envíelo hoy.
example.en: Sign the document and send it today.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone or something allows a person to perform an action?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a matching form of permitir, identify the allowed person with me, te, le, nos, os, or les, then keep the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The person marker comes before a finite form of permitir. Permitir changes for the subject and time, while the allowed action remains an -ar, -er, or -ir dictionary form: la llave me permite entrar.

example.es: El permiso les permitirá trabajar aquí.
example.en: The permit will allow them to work here.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: añadir soporte a + tecnología o función
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that technical compatibility is being added for something?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of añadir with soporte, then introduce the technology or feature with a; a pronoun such as le can stand for it.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Añadir changes for the person and time, while soporte names the new technical compatibility. If the receiving system is already clear, attach le to an unchanged infinitive: añadirle soporte.

example.es: Van a añadir soporte a ese formato.
example.en: They are going to add support for that format.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: puerto · hardware · software · proyecto · soporte · Linux
cardDefinitions.answerEn: a Linux user treats an implanted physical computer port as useful because a future software project might eventually make it work
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The patient knows that merely wiring a port to nerves cannot make the brain control devices. He still wants the hardware installed and trusts that an open-source software project will eventually add support. The surgeon recognizes this optimistic hardware-first attitude as characteristic of a Linux user; the official title text extends the joke with a Vista-Ready sticker.
